s1.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with skin lesions in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: tender annular erythematous plaques on the neck and trunk
abnormal laboratory findings including leukopenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia
key_facts: 10-day history of fever
tender lesions on the neck and trunk
past medical history of IgG-κ multiple myeloma
recent chemotherapy with ixazomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone
annular erythematous plaques with violaceous and crusted centers
white blood cell count: 2.3 × 10^3/μL
hemoglobin: 12.1 g/dL
platelet count: 29 × 10^3/μL
C-reactive protein: 3.31 mg/dL
blood culture: negative
skin biopsy showed inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells
immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and myeloperoxidase, negative for CD138

shortlist.label: Sweet syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: fever, tender skin lesions, and recent chemotherapy

shortlist.label: Neutrophilic eccrine hidradenitis
shortlist.why_kept: febrile illness, skin lesions, and recent chemotherapy

shortlist.label: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: history of multiple myeloma and skin lesions

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of fever, tender annular erythematous plaques with violaceous and crusted centers, and inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells on skin biopsy, along with recent chemotherapy and negative blood culture, is consistent with Sweet syndrome, a condition often associated with malignancies and chemotherapy.

rejected.label: Leukemia cutis
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of multiple myeloma, the skin biopsy findings of inflammatory infiltrate and immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and myeloperoxidase but negative for CD138 do not support leukemia cutis, which would typically show infiltration of malignant leukemic cells.
